A partir d’un système de supervision et par une présence permanente autour de la machine, vous êtes garant du bon fonctionnement des équipements et de la qualité du papier sécurisé

Diplômé d’un Bac/Bac+2 technique ou scientifique ou équivalent, vous justifiez d’une première expérience dans la conduite de machines automatisées. Vous avez déjà travaillé sur un process de production en continu et êtes à l’aise avec les supervisions industrielles et les systèmes de pilotage.

Cette expérience a été acquise idéalement dans un contexte où les contraintes qualité sont fortes et où la précision des réglages, la rigueur dans l’exécution des tâches sont indispensables à la bonne réalisation de la mission.

Nous recherchons sur ce poste une personne dotée d’un bon esprit d’équipe, méthodique et ayant une forte appétence pour les activités à composante technique et la concrétisation sur le terrain.

Vous êtes reconnu pour votre fiabilité et votre sens des responsabilités.

Les avantages à nous rejoindre : 

· Intégrer un site industriel à taille humaine, reconnu pour son savoir-faire d’exception.

· Travailler sur des équipements modernes et performants, dans des ateliers propres et entretenus.

· Percevoir une rémunération attractive : salaire fixe sur 13 mois, primes liées au horaires postés, prime de performance, intéressement et participation, PEE…

· Profiter de solutions de restauration accessibles également les nuits et les week-ends.

· Bénéficier de stabilité : CDI et planning établi à l’année.

Poste basé à Vic-le-Comte, au sud de Clermont Ferrand (63), à mi-chemin entre Paris et la Méditerranée, en plein cœur du Pays des volcans d’Auvergne.

- Maîtrise des appareils de mesure et capacité à gérer leur vérification ou leur étalonnage. 

- Bonnes connaissances des systèmes énergétiques et des procédés thermiques et mécaniques. 

- Connaissance des systèmes électriques BT/HT, UPS, groupes électrogènes et chaînes de distribution. 

- Connaissance des systèmes de refroidissement, groupes froid, free cooling et régulation. 

- Maîtrise des logiciels d'estimation des performances énergétiques, de calcul réglementaire du bilan thermique et de simulation thermique dynamique.

title: Tech Lead, Android Core Product - Geneva, Switzerland
description:
The mission of Speechify is to make sure that reading is never a barrier to learning.

Over 50 million people use Speechify’s text-to-speech products to turn whatever they’re reading – PDFs, books, Google Docs, news articles, websites – into audio, so they can read faster, read more, and remember more. Speechify’s text-to-speech reading products include its iOS app, Android App, Mac App, Chrome Extension, and Web App. Google recently named Speechify the Chrome Extension of the Year and Apple named Speechify its Design award winner for inclusivity for 2025.

Today, nearly 200 people around the globe work on Speechify in a 100% distributed setting – Speechify has no office. These include frontend and backend engineers, AI research scientists, and others from Amazon, Microsoft, and Google, leading PhD programs like Stanford, high growth startups like Stripe, Vercel, Bolt, and many founders of their own companies.

Overview 

With the growth of our Android app, being the most used text-to-speech app in the Play Store, we find the need for a Senior Android Engineer to help us support the new user base as well as work on new and exciting projects to push us forward. 

This is a key role and ideal for someone who thinks strategically, enjoys fast-paced environments, passionate about making product decisions, and has experience building great user experiences that delight users.

We are a flat organization that allows anyone to become a leader by showing excellent technical skills and delivering results consistently and fast. Work ethic, solid communication skills, and obsession with winning are paramount. 

Our interview process involves several technical interviews and we aim to complete them within 1 week. 

What Yo u’ ll Do 

- Owning major features and working closely with our design team - take ownership of features inside the app and become responsible of delivering high quality features

- Shape the future of our Android team

- Own, maintain and improve reliability metrics for key features

- Participate in discussions across different teams - Product, Design, Engineering

- Review pull requests, and support other teammates

- Handle critical issues or cope with unexpected challenges 

- Take ownership of feature releases and provide nightly builds for the QA team

An Ideal Candidate Should Have 

- 5+ years of software engineering experience

- Familiarity with Android components

- Experience building or contributing to at least one Android app

- Product design intuition and user empathy

- Drive to push the boundaries of Android UI/UX

- Understanding of the importance of tests and how to approach writing tests

- Self-drive to improve the app and codebase above and beyond what's outlined in the spec

- Rock solid experience with Kotlin, Kotlin Coroutines, Kotlin Flow, Dagger 2, MVVM, Clean Architecture, Background Services, Music Player Service, Android Animations, Jetpack Navigation, JUnit tests

- Excellent communication skills

- User oriented problem solving approach

- Driven with continuous feedback from leaders

Bonus: 

- Experience building, maintaining, or otherwise contributing to open source projects in Android

- Experience with iOS, Web or NodeJS

Technologies we use: 

- Kotlin

- Kotlin Coroutines

- Kotlin Flow

- Jetpack Navigation

- Dagger 2

- Room

- Custom Views, Canvas & Paint

- Jetpack Compose

- JUnit

What We offer :

- A fast-growing environment where you can help shape the company and product.

- An entrepreneurial-minded team that supports risk, intuition, and hustle.

- A hands-off management approach so you can focus and do your best work.

- An opportunity to make a big impact in a transformative industry.

- Competitive salaries, a friendly and laid-back atmosphere, and a commitment to building a great asynchronous culture.

- Opportunity to work on a life-changing product that millions of people use.

- Build products that directly impact and support people with learning differences like dyslexia, ADD, low vision, concussions, autism, and more.

- Work in one of the fastest growing sectors of tech, the intersection of artificial intelligence and audio.

The Switzerland Based Salary range for this role is: 30,000-160,000 USD/Year + Bonus + Stock depending on experience.

title: Product Marketing Manager in Legal Tech (Zurich)
description:
Description Legal AI content is turning into a commodity. Every vendor ships the same AI-generated blog posts and the same generic battlecards. We are transitioning into an AI-native company ourselves, and that changes what this role has to be. You would sit in the marketing department with a dotted line to the product department, but not as a traditional product marketer who ships a few blog posts and calls it enablement. Not as a pure thinker who never touches a sales deck. Instead, as one person who owns our voice and turns it into everything the company needs to win: the thesis that gets us cited, the sales slide that closes next week’s deal, and the briefing that gets a General Counsel to say yes. 

You will use AI tooling and agents to cover ground that used to take a small team, so you can spend your own time on the part that cannot be delegated: the thinking, the judgment, and the writing that actually changes someone’s mind. 

Your mission 1. Product Marketing & Market Intelligence 

- Drive go-to-market impact for launches and expansion, from plan to execution. 

- Own deep knowledge of our ICP and competitive landscape, and feed it back into the product and sales strategy. 

- Bring market and customer truth back to Product so we build what actually matters. 

- Work across Product, Marketing, Sales and leadership. You don’t sit in a silo. 

2. Positioning, Narrative & Thought Leadership 

- Own positioning: define what Legartis stands for, against which alternatives, for which buyer. 

- Develop and defend clear, evidence-backed points of view on where Legal AI is going. Not generic AI-created opinions, but real positions based on customer and buyer research (interviews with General Counsel, CFOs, legal operations leaders). 

- Conceive flagship studies and thought leadership content. Direct AI tools to help you scale production while you own the substance and the voice. 

- Own our thought leadership channels, including video, and decide what gets said. Write what can’t be delegated: founder posts, executive bylines, keynote scripts, board-level memos. 

3. Sales & Customer-Facing Enablement 

- Build the sales slides, briefings, one-pagers and competitive battlecards that make Sales and Customer Success more effective in every conversation. 

- Translate positioning and research into materials for specific deals, verticals and executive-level conversations. 

- Work directly with Sales and CS to find out what’s missing in the field. Build case studies and customer proof points that Sales actually uses, not ones that sit in a folder. 

What We Want to Achieve Together 

In 6 months: a flagship study that gets cited by competitors and customers. Sales armed with materials that actually get used in deals. A clear Legartis position that everyone in the company can repeat in 30 seconds. 

In 12 months: Legartis recognized as one of the leading European voices on Legal AI, with a content and enablement engine, you plus the AI tools you direct, that outproduces companies with five times the headcount. 

Your profile - Proven strategist: demonstrated success creating and executing marketing strategies. 

- Storyteller: you craft compelling materials about complex AI products for non-technical audiences. 

- Clear communicator: exceptional written and verbal communication with a strong visual sensibility. 

- Impact-driven: comfortable with experimentation and interpreting both quantitative and qualitative data. 

- AI-savvy: crafty with AI tools and automations — you use them daily and keep exploring what's new. 

- A track record where writing and thinking were central: journalism, industry or analyst research, strategy consulting, or senior product marketing with real strategic ownership. 4+ years in marketing, product marketing or a comparable strategic role at a SaaS company. Classic PMM experience (positioning, GTM, enablement) is a strong plus, not a hard requirement, if your thinking and writing are strong enough. 

- Fluent German and English, executive-level writing in both. 

Why us? - Real editorial ownership over our voice and our position, not a content calendar handed down from someone else. 

- A platform to build your own visible profile as a voice in Legal AI. 

- Modern office in Leipzig or Berlin, hybrid setup, with regular presence in Zürich and team events such as hiking, dinners and offsites. 

- Employee Stock Ownership Plan (ESOP) participation. 

- Competitive salary, based on experience and seniority. 

Process - 30 min with our People & Operations Manager: cultural fit, understanding the role and your expectations. 

- Positioning conversation with our Head of Product: bring a point of view on Legal AI and be ready to defend it live. 

- Case study: show us something you’ve written or built, and how you’d turn it into a sales-ready asset. 

- Meet the team in the office. 

- Decision: if it’s mutual, we welcome you to the team! 

How to Apply 

Send us your CV, two or three writing or work samples you’re proud of, and a short note answering: what’s your sharpest point of view on where Legal AI is heading, and what’s the evidence?

title: Legal AI Engineer (Zurich)
description:
Description Legartis is on a mission: to unlock legal work at scale.

We set the standard for AI-powered contract work by offering a platform that changes how legal teams work, from drafting through negotiation to completion. We are now looking for the person who turns what customers actually need into what our AI actually does.

Joining Legartis is not taking a job, you take ownership. We are a team of product builders and lawyers, who do not chase hype; we build substance. If you are a lawyer who builds, someone who has stopped waiting for better tools and started making them, this is your moment and your place.

Send us your CV, a short note on why Legartis, and links to anything you have built or published.

Your mission Most companies split this seat across three teams, and that split is exactly the problem. The person who hears the customer describe their workflow should be the person who writes the requirement, and the person who writes the requirement should be able to build the first version themselves. That is you.

1. You translate customer reality into engineering requirements — and into revenue. You sit in customer and expert calls alongside Sales, not as a note-taker but as the person who understands the legal work. In trials and hackathons you coach hands-on: the customer drives, you navigate, and they create the first "wow" moment themselves. When they say "that won't work for us" or "we'll build it ourselves", you answer with a concrete path (a workaround, a workflow, the honest maintenance cost of the alternative) and you leave every conversation with a next step: trial licenses, a hackathon, a scoped rollout. Then you pull out the workflow: what actually happens, in what order, where it breaks, what the customer would pay to never do again. And you write the spec, edge cases, and acceptance criteria that Engineering can build against.

2. You build the skills yourself. You write, test, and ship agent skills and playbooks that solve real customer workflows. You build the evaluation frameworks and test sets that prove they got better rather than just different. When the AI fails on a clause, you diagnose why, at the prompt and context level, and you either fix it or hand Engineering a diagnosis precise enough to act on.

3. You make it repeatable, and therefore sellable. Anything you build once for one customer, you turn into something Sales and Customer Success can run without you. Standard demo environments. A skill library they can reach for. Onboarding that lands in days rather than months. Where Customer Success needs legal depth you step in, fix it, and turn the fix into something the team can handle alone next time. Your success is measured by how rarely you need to be in the room, and by what happens to adoption and expansion when you are not.

4. You are the legal authority in the building. Legal and compliance questions land with you: contract reviews, customer security and data protection questions, the occasional in-house matter which makes roughly ten to fifteen percent of your time. You use our own product to do it, and you tell us honestly when it is not good enough.

Your profile The person we picture. There is a name emerging for what we are describing, and it is not "lawyer who is good with computers". It is legal quant : a lawyer who builds their own tooling to practise law, rather than waiting for a vendor to ship it. The distinction that matters to us: plenty of lawyers now use AI. A legal quant builds with it. They look at a workflow and ask how to redesign it from first principles to get the best possible outcome, rather than making the existing process incrementally faster.

A note on how we are weighting this role. Three capabilities make someone exceptional here: commercial instinct, legal depth, and technical ability to build. The ideal candidate has all three. We know that person is rare, and we are not going to pretend otherwise by writing a wish list and hoping. So for this role we weight the technical evidence most heavily, because it is the hardest of the three to teach on the job.

If you believe you genuinely combine all three, we want to talk to you regardless of how neatly your CV matches the bullets below. Say so in your note and tell us what you have built and what you have sold.

1. Technical track record. You have built things and they exist and ideally you have published some of it. You are fluent with LLMs the way a practitioner is fluent, not a spectator: you know how context windows fail you or why a prompt stopped working. When something breaks you go into the system rather than around it. Scripting, Git, and APIs are a strong plus.

2. Legal foundation. A law degree with a commercial-contracts focus: German-qualified (Bachelor, Master, or Staatsexamen) or an equivalent qualification from another jurisdiction. No bar admission required, no second Staatsexamen required. What we need: you have worked hands-on with German commercial contracts, drafting, reviewing, and negotiating them, and you can hold a conversation with a General Counsel as a peer.

3. Commercial and entrepreneurial track record. You have carried commercial responsibility for something of your own: a freelance client base, a legal tech product, or a company you started. You know what it takes to win a client from a standing start and why "they did not understand the value" is never the customer's fault. If instead you have supported enterprise sales teams in demos, pilots, and expert calls, tell us what you changed about the outcome.

You prioritise by impact, you are comfortable deciding without permission, and you would rather ship something imperfect this week than something elegant next quarter.

4. Language. Excellent German and English. German is non-negotiable: our customers are DACH legal teams and the nuance lives in their language. You can run a room of legal buyers, ask the sharp question, and write a specification precise enough to build from. Other EU languages are a plus.

Why us? - Impact over hype. You define a new discipline at the intersection of law, product, and AI. Your work directly shapes how thousands of legal professionals will operate.
- No silos. You sit between Product, Engineering, and the customer, with a direct line to all three. The better argument wins, not the higher title.
- We invest in you. The enterprise motion (multi-stakeholder pilots, procurement cycles, security reviews) is teachable, and we teach it: side by side in real customer calls from week one.
- Real ownership. Competitive salary and employee stock options (ESOP).
- Build in public. We want you to keep publishing what you build, because it makes you better and it makes us visible.
- Offices in Berlin, Leipzig, and Zurich with a flexible hybrid setup. Regular apéros, lunches, and hiking trips as we enjoy the journey together.

Process - Expectations. A conversation with the People Manager about the role and who you are.
- Depth. A conversation with our General Counsel & Head of Legal AI on Legal Engineering at Legartis and where the legal market is going.
- Build session. A live case at the intersection of legal reasoning, prompting, and product work: a real customer scenario, a legal AI workflow, or a playbook that misbehaves.
- Meet the team in our Zurich office.
- A mutual decision, before we welcome you to the team.

description:

- Du gestaltest Kundentermine, Workshops und Angebotsphasen in unseren Fokusbranchen Industrial Manufacturing, High Tech, Defence und Automotive

- Du übernimmst Verantwortung in komplexen Vertriebs- und Transformationssituationen und bringst Markt-, Branchen- und Kundenimpulse aktiv ein.

Dein Profil Die Anforderungen: 
- Du verfügst über ein tiefes Verständnis der Prozesse in der diskreten Fertigung und kennst die Anforderungen produzierender Unternehmen.
- Du bringst Erfahrung in mindestens einer unserer Fokusbranchen mit: Industrial Manufacturing, High Tech, Defense oder Automotive.
- Du hast fundierte SAP-Erfahrung aus der Beratung oder aus einem Industrieunternehmen und bewegst dich sicher in Transformationskontexten.
- Du verstehst die Zusammenhänge zwischen Produktion, Supply Chain, Digitalisierung und SAP S/4HANA.
- Du hast idealerweise bereits als Projektleiter:in, Teilprojektleiter:in oder Stream Lead Verantwortung übernommen.
- Du kannst komplexe Anforderungen strukturiert erfassen, in verständliche Lösungsszenarien übersetzen und diese sicher auf Deutsch und Englisch vermitteln.

Warum wir? Was Du unter anderem von uns erwarten kannst: 
- Attraktives Gehalt
- Sicherer Arbeitsplatz in einem wachstumsstarken Unternehmen
- Flexible Arbeitszeiten mit Homeoffice-Option
- Angenehme Arbeitsatmosphäre und gute Führungskultur (kaum messbare Mitarbeiterfluktuation)
- Flache Hierarchien und kurze Entscheidungswege
- Firmenwagen und moderne IT-Ausstattung
- Fachliche und persönliche Weiterbildungsmöglichkeiten
Lerne ein Unternehmen kennen, in dem Menschen gut und gerne zusammenarbeiten – und finde hier weitere Benefits, die wir dir bieten.
Du erkennst dich in der Beschreibung wieder? Dann zögere nicht und nimm am besten noch heute Kontakt auf. Gerne können wir uns über diese Stelle und deine Möglichkeiten bei GAMBIT unterhalten.
Wir erwarten nicht, dass alle Kandidat:innen in allen genannten Bereichen gleich qualifiziert sind. Nenn uns daher gerne weitere, hier nicht genannte Fähigkeiten und Erfahrungen, über die du verfügst und die für diese Stelle möglicherweise relevant sein könnten.
Ganz besonders wichtig ist uns, dass unsere Mitarbeiter:innen unser Verständnis von Arbeit und Zusammenarbeit teilen. Denn Arbeit ist für uns mehr als nur ein Job, Zusammenarbeit mehr als nur ein Nebeneinander. Wir legen Wert auf einen respektvollen, wertschätzenden Umgang, Fairness und einen offenen Dialog.

title: Enterprise Account Executive - Spanish -Speaking  - London, UK
description:
About Pallet 

Pallet is building AI Agents to transform the physical economy — a $12 trillion global industry. We’ve raised $50M from top investors, including General Catalyst, Bessemer Venture Partners, and Bain Capital Ventures. In under two years, we’ve achieved 700% revenue growth and are just getting started.

Our mission is to increase the efficiency of the global supply chain by automating the manual workflows that slow supply chain teams down — from scheduling and appointment setting to data entry and load management. Our flagship platform provides end-to-end visibility, control, and optimization, while our newest product, CoPallet, introduces AI Agents that can understand and execute requests in real time and integrate directly with customer systems.

As companies across the physical economy look to generative AI to drive efficiency, many are turning to Pallet to lead the way. With deep supply chain expertise and cutting-edge AI capabilities, we’re positioned to build the next $10B company powering the physical economy.

Join us and work alongside leaders from Google, DoorDash, YC, and more to shape the future of supply chain technology.

London, United Kingdom or Zurich, Switzerland (Remote to start, transitioning to 5 days/week in-office once our local office opens) 

You could be an Enterprise Account Executive anywhere. Why us? 

- Join a well-funded, high-growth startup on a clear path to $100M ARR.

- Sell a category-defining AI Agents platform with massive surface area across logistics.

- Build Pallet’s presence across Europe as one of the first commercial hires on the ground.

- Work directly with founders and senior leadership to define our international go-to-market strategy.

- Help transform one of the world’s largest industries while building toward a $10B+ outcome.

About the opportunity 

We’re hiring our first Enterprise Account Executives in EMEA to build Pallet’s commercial presence across Europe.

You’ll own net-new enterprise acquisition across the region, build relationships with the largest logistics providers in Europe, and help establish the playbook for our international expansion. This is a highly consultative enterprise sales role focused on educating customers on an entirely new category of AI-powered workflow automation.

You’ll partner closely with Sales, Product, Engineering, Solutions, and Customer Success to drive a solution-selling motion centered around workflow discovery, AI use case identification, structured pilots, and measurable ROI.

Initially, this role will be remote from London while we establish our UK presence. Once our London office opens, this role will transition to working from the office five days per week when not traveling to customer sites.

How you will make an impact 

- Own the full enterprise sales cycle across EMEA, from outbound prospecting through contract signature.

- Build and maintain a 3x-4x qualified pipeline through disciplined outbound execution while self-sourcing at least 30% of opportunities.

- Develop relationships with executive stakeholders across Europe’s largest logistics providers, including COO, CIO, VP Operations, VP Supply Chain, and VP Technology.

- Lead consultative discovery sessions that map operational workflows to Pallet’s AI agent capabilities.

- Scope and lead structured pilots that demonstrate measurable operational ROI and convert into enterprise deployments.

- Build executive business cases that align operational improvements with financial outcomes.

- Document repeatable customer use cases and market feedback to shape Pallet’s product roadmap and international GTM strategy.

- Help establish Pallet as the leading AI platform for enterprise logistics across Europe.

What we’re looking for 

- 8+ years of enterprise B2B SaaS or enterprise logistics sales experience.

- Business-fluent Spanish you can run discovery, negotiate and present to executives in Spanish. 

- Proven track record of consistently closing six- and seven-figure enterprise software agreements.

- Strong consultative selling and value-based sales methodology.

- Experience navigating complex buying committees and long enterprise sales cycles.

- Executive presence with senior operators and technology leaders.

- Comfortable selling technical, workflow-heavy software products.

- Ability to quickly understand complex logistics operations and translate them into compelling AI automation opportunities.

- Excellent outbound prospecting and territory-building discipline.

- Willingness to travel extensively across Europe.

Experience selling into logistics, supply chain, transportation, or warehouse operations is strongly preferred but not required. Candidates without logistics experience should demonstrate an ability to quickly learn operational workflows and become trusted advisors to customers.

Working model 

Working hours are generally 9:00am-6:00pm London time , providing full coverage of the European business day while maintaining regular collaboration with our San Francisco headquarters.

You’ll typically spend:

- Mornings and early afternoons working directly with European customers and prospects.

- Late afternoons collaborating with our US-based Sales, Product, and Engineering teams during our daily overlap window.

- Approximately 75% of your time traveling across Europe for customer meetings, executive workshops, pilots, and industry events.

Initially this role will be remote. Once Pallet opens its local office, you’ll work from the office five days per week whenever you’re not traveling to customers.

Reporting structure 

You’ll report directly to the General Manager, London for territory strategy, customer relationships, and international expansion.

You’ll also work closely with our Head of Sales , participating in weekly pipeline reviews, forecasting, and sales process alignment with the US team.

Interview Process 

- Chat with Christy - Business Recruiter - 30 mins

- Deal Review - 30 mins

- Discovery Mock Interview - 45-60 mins

- Final Interview - ~3 hours

- Brief Background Check and Reference Check

We move fast, and we’ll keep you informed at every stage of the process.

Compensation 

The estimated compensation range for this role is £100,000-£240,000 OTE , depending on experience and skill set.

Our compensation follows a standard 50/50 enterprise sales structure consisting of base salary and target commission. High performers are eligible for uncapped commission accelerators above quota.

In addition to cash compensation, we offer competitive equity, benefits, and significant growth opportunities as one of our earliest international commercial hires.

Final compensation will be determined based on experience, qualifications, and demonstrated enterprise sales performance.

Our Benefits 

We invest in our people the same way we invest in our product: seriously.

- 🩺 Health, Vision, and Dental benefits 

- 🏝️ Take-what-you-need Paid Vacation

- ➕ Life Insurance and Accidental Insurance 

- ❤️‍🩹 Short-Term Disability Coverage

- 💸 Generous salary and equity for all staff

- 🪜 401k option; helping you save for the future

- 🧑‍🧑‍🧒‍🧒 Paid parental leave to support growing families

- 📚 Yearly learning and development stipend

- 🚌 Commuter benefits for Bay Area employees

- 🚘 Uber ride stipend if you ever have to work late in the office 

- 🏡 Remote office home stipend to get you comfy in your space

- 🍔 Daily catered lunches provided 

- ✈️ Onboarding trip to San Francisco HQ if you work remotely

- 🥤 Monthly happy hours

- 🎉 Annual Company Offsites; our last one was in Palm Springs CA 🌴

Workplace Policy 

We are an in-person company. Our offices in San Francisco, New York City and London are where ideas get built, decisions get made, and the team gets stronger. We have invested in making them genuinely great places to spend your day, with catered lunches, monthly happy hours, and people who care about the work and each other.

Most of our team works in office five days a week. For select roles, we hire remotely across the U.S. Remote employees come to one of our offices for their first week to onboard and meet the team, and we cover the full trip. 

Every role is different. Travel expectations are always shared upfront in the job description and confirmed in your first call with us.

Equal Opportunity 

Pallet is an Equal Opportunity Employer. We make all employment decisions based solely on merit. We provide equal employment opportunities to all applicants and employees without discrimination on the basis of race, religion, color, national origin, gender (including pregnancy, childbirth, or related medical conditions), sexual orientation, gender identity, gender expression, age, status as a protected veteran, disability status, or any other applicable legally protected characteristic. We prohibit any form of discrimination or harassment. This policy applies to all terms and conditions of employment, including hiring.

Candidate Privacy Notice 

Please review Pallet’s Candidate Privacy Notice here .

Accommodations 

Pallet complies with the Americans with Disabilities Act (ADA), as amended by the ADA Amendments Act, and all applicable state or local laws. We will reasonably accommodate qualified individuals with a disability during the application process and throughout employment as required by law.

If you need any assistance or accommodations due to a disability, please contact us at Find Jobs in Switzerland on Arbeitnow

title: Director, International Privacy Lead and Data Protection Officer
description:
Director, International Privacy Lead & Data Protection Officer 

Overview 

Alnylam is seeking an experienced privacy and data protection leader to serve as Director, International Privacy Lead & Data Protection Officer. Reporting to the Senior Director, Head of Privacy, AI Governance, Training & Communications within Ethics & Compliance, this role will lead Alnylam’s international privacy program, with primary responsibility for Europe (EU/EEA, United Kingdom, and Switzerland) and support for broader international markets.

As Alnylam’s formally appointed Data Protection Officer (DPO) under applicable European and Swiss privacy laws, the Director will provide independent privacy oversight, advise the business on data protection obligations, and maintain direct access and escalation channels to senior leadership for material privacy risks.

This individual contributor will be expected to serve as a proactive partner to the our international business, anticipating privacy and data protection obligations driven by regulatory change and business growth, and translating those requirements into actionable guidance for policies, operations and ways of working.

The successful candidate will partner closely with Legal, Information Security, IT, HR, Commercial, Medical Affairs, Clinical Development, Pharmacovigilance, Procurement, Ethics & Compliance, and other business stakeholders to enable responsible use of personal data while strengthening privacy governance, risk management, and business adoption across international markets.

Hybrid role preferably based in Zug, Switzerland. Also open to candidates based in Madrid, Spain or Maidenhead, UK.

Responsibilities 

- Lead and mature Alnylam’s international privacy program, with primary focus on Europe and support for broader international markets, by setting program priorities, strengthening governance frameworks, and ensuring privacy requirements are embedded into business planning, policies, controls, and day-to-day operations.

- Serve as Alnylam’s appointed DPO under EU GDPR, UK GDPR, and applicable Swiss data protection requirements, providing independent advice, monitoring compliance, maintaining required independence, and acting as the primary point of contact for supervisory authorities and data subjects.

- Oversee privacy risk identification, assessment, mitigation, monitoring, and escalation processes, including privacy-by-design and privacy-by-default requirements, DPIAs, TIAs, Records of Processing Activities (ROPA), cross-border transfer assessments, and related governance documentation.

- Advise business and functional leaders on privacy requirements related to clinical research, pharmacovigilance, commercial operations, medical affairs, human resources, patient support programs, real-world evidence, AI, and other data-driven initiatives.

- Partner with Information Security, Legal, Procurement, and business stakeholders on privacy incident response, breach assessment, third-party privacy risk management, data protection terms, data sharing arrangements, remediation, and regulatory notification decisions.

- Proactively monitor the European and international privacy, AI, digital, cyber and data governance legislative landscape, anticipating compliance impacts from business growth and regulatory change, and rapidly translating new or changing requirements into practical updates to policies, controls, business processes, training, and operational guidance.

- Develop and deliver privacy training, communications, awareness initiatives, metrics, monitoring activities, and continuous improvement plans that promote a culture of privacy and accountability across international markets.

Qualifications 

Required 

- Juris Doctor (JD), LLM, or other advanced legal degree required.

- 12+ years of privacy legal or compliance experience at a law firm and/or in-house.

- Significant experience advising on privacy risk in regulated life sciences settings, including clinical research, pharmacovigilance, medical affairs, commercial, HR, patient-facing, and digital activities.

- Experience serving as a DPO or advising in an equivalent independent oversight capacity for GDPR, UK GDPR, Swiss FADP, or comparable privacy regimes.

- Deep understanding of GDPR, UK GDPR, Swiss FADP, international data transfer requirements, and global privacy regulations.

- Experience advising on AI, data-driven innovation, real-world evidence, cross-border data use, and other strategic privacy initiatives.

- Strong privacy governance and risk management experience, including the ability to set priorities, mature program controls, and translate complex requirements into practical guidance for technical and non-technical audiences.

- Strong executive communication, stakeholder management, and influencing skills, with the credibility and judgment to engage senior leaders, regulators, external partners, and cross-functional stakeholders.

- Proven ability to lead complex privacy initiatives across matrixed, international organizations, applying practical and proportionate judgment to ambiguous issues.

- Executive presence, regulatory credibility, and strategic judgment to anticipate legal, business, and technology shifts and translate them into clear priorities for the international privacy program.

Preferred 

- Privacy certifications such as CIPP/E, CIPM, CIPT, AIGP, or similar credentials preferred.

- Experience interacting directly with European data protection authorities and regulators preferred.

- Experience leading multinational privacy teams or global privacy programs preferred.

- International business experience within a global life sciences organization preferred.

About Alnylam: Alnylam Pharmaceuticals (Nasdaq: ALNY) has led the translation of RNA interference (RNAi) into a whole new class of innovative medicines with the potential to transform the lives of people afflicted with rare and more prevalent diseases. Based on Nobel Prize-winning science, RNAi therapeutics represent a powerful, clinically validated approach to treating diseases at their genetic source by “interfering” with mRNA that cause or contribute to disease. Since our founding in 2002, Alnylam has led the RNAi Revolution and continues to turn scientific possibility into reality.

Our culture: Our people-first culture is guided by our core values: fiercely innovative, open culture, purposeful urgency, passion for excellence, and commitment to people, and these values influence how we work and the business decisions we make. Thanks to feedback from our employees over the years, we’ve been fortunate to be named a top employer around the world. By empowering employees to embrace their unique differences at work, our business grows stronger with advanced and original thinking, allowing us to bring groundbreaking medicines to patients.

title: Infrastructure Software Engineer
description:
Join our mission 

We're proud to work with many incredible companies, accelerating their ability to build their products. 

We've spent years watching talented engineering teams lose momentum to the same frustrating bottleneck: waiting. Waiting for CI to finish. Waiting for builds to complete. Waiting for tests to run.

After experiencing this pain firsthand at companies of every size, we set out to build the developer infrastructure platform we'd always wanted to use. Something that would seamlessly integrate with our workflows and the tools teams already love—but make everything dramatically faster and more cost-effective.

Today, we're already accelerating hundreds of companies around the world, helping them ship features instead of waiting for infrastructure. We've built something that feels almost magical in its simplicity: change your runs-on line, mount your toolchain cache directory and suddenly your builds are 5x faster.

About the role 

Namespace's approach is low-friction, designed for immediate integration into existing developer toolchains, empowering teams to experience tangible results within just five minutes. With an end-to-end stack optimized for high performance—including compute, memory, storage, and networking—Namespace delivers capabilities and efficiencies unmatched by traditional cloud providers.

Own the software that drives our hardware. You'll write the control planes, automation, and observability that keep our global fleet fast, efficient, and reliable, while charting a path to scale that continues to increase the number of "machines under management" per engineer.

Our culture 

We're looking for people with grit—people who push through ambiguity, take ownership, and keep going when things get hard. You're deeply curious, driven to understand how things work and how they can be improved. Most importantly, you have a strong bias to execution: you don't wait for perfect conditions, you ship, learn, and iterate quickly. If you care about building, moving fast, and making real impact, you'll fit right in.

What you'll do 

- Manage and automate the fleet – build services for provisioning, health checks, upgrades, and incident remediation

- Uphold reliability – embed observability, graceful degradation, and rollback paths into every layer you touch

- Architect the network – design and evolve a high-throughput, low-latency fabric tailored to our high performance use-cases

- Ship software, not scripts – develop clean, testable code (mostly Go) that treats our fleet like a first-class API

- Drive efficiency – improve utilization and power-to-performance ratios so capacity grows slower than usage

- Partner across the stack – work with product, infra, and platform teams to scope and deliver features like storage-aware scheduling, cache volumes, and other developer-facing features

What we're looking for 

- Proven experience engineering large-scale infrastructure - writing the software that runs fleets, not just operating existing hyperscalers

- Depth in network architecture, data-center design, and performance tuning

- Hands-on time deploying and managing compute hardware at scale (servers, switches, etc)

- Fluency with modern orchestration and automation tooling (Kubernetes, Terraform, Ansible - plus the judgment to know when to build vs. buy)

- A track record of delivering reliable systems and measurable efficiency gains

You can expect: 

- Competitive salary and stock options

- Flexible working hours

- Market-leading parental leave

Life at Namespace Labs: 

- We pride ourselves in being a small team of experts that can achieve a lot.

- We balance our long-term vision with short-term pragmatism.

- We believe in being fully transparent internally on how decisions are made, on how the company is doing, and we use that information to drive our decisions.

The Role

You will own the research question at the centre of LEA, our foundation model of the physical world: can a model learn what normally happens on a site, by place, hour and weather, so that an anomaly is simply what it did not expect? The first version is a probabilistic memory of each site. The next is a world model across every site that predicts the next state in latent space, starting from open world-model weights and growing on field data nobody else holds.

Our robots and cameras run on live security sites around the clock, and every event is kept with its clip, the model's verdict and the operator's outcome. That record is your dataset. You will work alongside our perception and model engineers, and your results go into production, not only into papers.

What You'll Work On

- Site memory: a learned, probabilistic model of each site: which people, vehicles and robots are where, at what hour, in what weather, and how the scene usually unfolds.

- Anomaly as surprise: replace rule-based alerting with measured surprise, and work out how to evaluate it when real incidents are rare.

- World model: post-train open world-model weights on aligned multi-sensor field sequences, JEPA-style, predicting in latent space rather than pixels.

- Transfer: from one site's memory to a model of all of them, and representations that carry across sites and domains.

title: Controller
description:
About Notabene

Notabene is building infrastructure that's transforming how money moves in the digital economy. We're evolving beyond our compliance foundations to enable the next generation of digital financial services between regulated institutions with unprecedented efficiency. With nearly 50 employees across 14 countries and having recently closed our Series B round last November with support from leading investors including Y Combinator, DRW, F-Prime, Jump Capital, Castle Island, and Green Visor Capital, we're looking for people like you to help shape the future rails of the crypto industry.

Location: 

US-based, Remote East Coast

The impact you will have

Notabene is planning on going through its first external financial statement audit, covering the fiscal years ending January 2026 and January 2027. You will own that process. You will also own the close, the books, and the accounting policy for a two-entity, multi-currency business whose revenue includes subscription fees, usage-based transaction billing, and a payments network take rate that has no clean accounting precedent anywhere.

The accounting function is already substantially built. Close runs, the books are in order, and readiness work for the audit is well underway. What we need is someone to own it, finish it, and take it through the audit, while raising the standard on policy and documentation as the business gets more complex. You will be the most senior accounting voice in the company, reporting to the VP of Finance, with one direct report and a set of external providers. You will not have a large team before late 2027, and that is deliberate. Capacity here comes from better systems and better automation, and you will be the one deciding what those look like.

Within a year you are successful if

- Notabene has a clean audit opinion on both fiscal years, with no material weaknesses and no second cycle on auditor requests

- The close hits its calendar consistently, starting with the revenue close landing on time

- Revenue recognition is documented in a written memo that stands up in fieldwork, rather than living only in the billing system configuration

- Multi-entity consolidation and FX translation run cleanly enough to survive audit scrutiny, with intercompany and CTA tied and supported

- Payroll allocation across departments and software development capitalization are written policy applied consistently, not judgment applied after the fact

- Key accounting controls are documented, operating, and evidenced

- At least two accounting processes that are manual today run without a person in the loop, and still hold up under audit

What you will be doing

Audit. Run the readiness assessment, build the remediation plan, contribute the technical view on which firm we engage, and then own the auditor relationship day to day.

Close and reporting. Own the monthly, quarterly, and annual close across Notabene Inc. and Notabene GmbH. Produce GAAP financial statements, consolidations, intercompany eliminations, and FX translation under ASC 830.

Technical accounting. Write the positions and the memos. ASC 606 across three revenue models, ASC 350-40 for internal-use software capitalization, ASC 718 for stock compensation expense, and whatever emerges as stablecoin payment revenue matures.

Revenue and billing systems. Own Tabs as the billing and revenue system of record, including contract configuration, usage data integrity, and the bridge from Tabs to the general ledger.

Cost accounting. Build the payroll allocation method for people whose work splits across functions, and the capitalization policy for development work, so departmental margin reflects where effort actually goes.

Controls. Design and implement controls over revenue, cash, procure to pay, and payroll. Not SOX. Controls that operate, are evidenced, and can be walked by an auditor.

Automation. Evaluate the accounting stack and the processes running on it with a bias toward automation, including agentic tooling where work is rule-bound and high volume. Categorization, reconciliation matching, usage validation, and collections follow-up are the obvious places to start.

Accounting operations. Own AR and collections with your direct report, plus AP and payroll accounting. Employee onboarding and HRIS administration sit with People, not with you.

Tax. Own US tax compliance in coordination with our external advisers, including the income tax provision and sales tax. Coordinate Swiss compliance with our local accountants.

External providers. We produce revenue in-house, our Swiss accountants produce their piece, and our outsourced firm assembles the close. You will own the checklist, the policies, and the reconciliations, so providers execute against a Notabene-owned close rather than holding it themselves.

- You have taken a company through a first external audit and can describe specifically what broke and what you did about it

- Swiss entity experience, including CHF functional currency and Swiss statutory or VAT exposure

- Digital assets, payments, or regulated financial services exposure

title: Manufacturing Quality Engineer
description:
Gravis Robotics is a high-growth Series A start-up backed by SoftBank, bringing Physical AI to the construction industry, turning heavy construction machines into autonomous robots. 

Gravis began as an ETH Zurich spin-out, and our unique combination of learning-based automation and augmented remote control lets one operator safely conduct a fleet of earthmoving machines in a gamified environment. 

Backed by deep robotics research and now deployed across multiple countries with leading construction and equipment partners, our team is rapidly growing to bring this technology to a trillion-dollar industry. 

The Gravis RACK is a machine-agnostic retrofit kit that adds autonomy to excavators and wheel loaders from 10 to 100+ tonnes: LiDAR and camera sensing, GNSS RTK, networking hardware and rugged edge compute that works offline. Paired with the Slate tablet and our Copilot software, it lets an operator run a machine manually, with AI assistance, or fully autonomously. Increasingly, we also build custom hardware to adapt our machines for highly specialized, robust applications beyond traditional excavation. 

About the role 

We are looking for a manufacturing quality engineer to own the quality and reliability of the Gravis hardware package that turns regular excavators into awesome, autonomous machines. You will work with our engineering and production team in Zurich defining and implementing quality measures like incoming inspections, supply chain validations, failure analysis and product return teardowns to enable our custom AI hardware a safe and reliable operation of heavy machines. You are capable of working both independently and with others, and are intrinsically driven to solve challenging applied problems with a rigorous attention to detail and an exploratory imagination.

You are our first quality hire. There is no dedicated quality team, no lab, and no playbook; you will design the test / fixture / process and then go build it. 

What you will do 

- Define what hardware quality means for Gravis from ground up

- Design and implement testing systems, jigs and fixtures from incoming inspection to product shipping

- Document failures, root causes and mitigations, build a failure database and review regularly with design and production

- Teardown and analysis of field returns, drive corrective actions

- Own supplier quality: first article inspection, qualification, audits, and 8D follow-through

- Tighten drawings and specifications; critical characteristics, unambiguous acceptance criteria

- Help building our long-term reliability and environmental test strategy as we scale

What we're looking for 

- A university degree in mechanical, electrical, quality Engineering or equivalent practical experience

- 3+ years experience in quality / manufacturing engineering in low volume manufacturing

- Hands on failure analysis and teardowns

- CAD knowledge for designing fixtures

- Experience in hand metrology

- Solid understanding of mechanical and electrical systems

- Good command of English, both written and spoken

Beneficial skills 

- Experience in GD&T

- Experience in SQL / python

- Exposure to environmental / accelerated lifetime testing (e.g. vibration, shock, ingress, UV)

- Fluency in Mandarin

- Off-highway, agricultural, mining or other harsh-environment equipment 

This is an opportunity to join a dynamic, multidisciplinary team and to be part of a company that is reshaping heavy construction.

Gravis is an equal opportunity employer. description:

IonQ’s newest generation of quantum computers, the IonQ Tempo, is the latest in a line of cutting-edge systems that have been helping customers and partners including Amazon Web Services, and AstraZeneca achieve 20x performance results and accelerate innovation in drug discovery, materials science, financial modeling, logistics, cybersecurity, and defense. Headquartered in College Park, Maryland, IonQ has operations in California, Colorado, Massachusetts, Tennessee, Washington, Italy, South Korea, Sweden, Switzerland, Canada, and the United Kingdom. Our quantum computing services are available through all major cloud providers, while we also meet the needs of networking and sensing customers across land, sea, air, and space. IonQ is making quantum platforms more accessible and impactful than ever before. 

Location: This role is based onsite in Geneva, Switzerland.
Travel: 
Job ID: 1892 

ID Quantique (IDQ), part of IonQ, is a global leader in quantum-safe communications. We provide solutions to protect governments, telecommunication infrastructures, and banking & financial institutions from the “harvest-now, decrypt-later” threat, delivering both terrestrial and space-based quantum-safe networks in live operation globally.

The Role: 

We are looking for a Principal Engineer to own the classical cryptography architecture of our post-quantum cryptography (PQC) hardware acceleration products, targeting hardware security module (HSM) and network-appliance applications. Real-world quantum-safe systems are hybrid systems: classical and post-quantum algorithms operating side by side, with careful key management, crypto agility and migration paths. You will be the senior authority for this classical and hybrid layer, working alongside our PQC architecture leadership. The role demands fluency on both sides of the transition: deep classical mastery combined with a solid working command of the post-quantum algorithms and standards the products are built around.

Responsibilities :

You will own the architecture and implementation strategy of the classical cryptographic functions of the product line: symmetric ciphers and modes (AES/GCM and beyond), hash functions (SHA-2/SHA-3, HMAC/KDF constructions), RSA/ECC offload, and true random number generation and entropy architecture (SP 800-90A/B/C). You will define the hybrid classical/post-quantum schemes (key establishment, dual signatures, composite certificates) and the crypto-agility mechanisms that allow customers to migrate safely, track the standardisation of hybrid and composite approaches (NIST guidance, IETF work on hybrid key establishment in TLS 1.3 and IKEv2, composite certificates) together with our PQC architects, guide RTL and software engineers implementing classical cores, technically evaluate third-party IP, and support FIPS 140-3 and CAVP certification of the classical algorithm suite. You will also own key-management and key-hierarchy architecture across the product, ensuring interoperability with deployed HSM, TLS and IPsec ecosystems.

- Own the classical and hybrid cryptography architecture of the product line: symmetric, hash, RSA/ECC, entropy and key management, and classical/PQC hybrid schemes

- Define crypto-agility and migration mechanisms that let customers move to quantum-safe deployments without breaking existing infrastructure

Requirements: 

We are looking for a candidate with a Master’s or PhD in Cryptography, Computer Science, Electrical Engineering or a related field and at least twelve years of experience implementing and architecting classical cryptography in real products, in hardware, software or both. You have deep command of symmetric and asymmetric primitives, modes of operation, key management and entropy generation, and you have taken cryptographic subsystems through FIPS 140-3 or Common Criteria evaluation. You also bring a solid working knowledge of the NIST post-quantum algorithms (ML-KEM, ML-DSA, SLH-DSA) and their deployment constraints: you do not need to be a lattice specialist, but you must be able to architect hybrid schemes with one.

You understand the practical constraints of deployed security infrastructure (HSMs, PKI, TLS and IPsec ecosystems) and how hybrid classical/post-quantum schemes are standardised and deployed in practice. You write precise specifications, guide implementers effectively, and make sound architecture decisions under real-world interoperability constraints. Fluency in English is required; French or German is an advantage.

- Proven architect of classical cryptographic subsystems with certification experience (FIPS 140-3, CAVP, Common Criteria)

- Practical knowledge of hybrid classical/PQC schemes, crypto agility and key-management architecture, with working command of the NIST PQC standards

Preferred Qualifications:

You believe that quantum-safe security is only as strong as the classical foundations it stands on. You enjoy being the guardian of correctness and interoperability in a programme pushing new technology, and you take pride in migrations that customers barely notice because they simply work.

Join our mission to deliver peace of mind at scale. Work with and learn from our Founder team that created over €1.5B in Fintech enterprise value and is driven to aim higher this time. - Challenger Mindset : Skilled at teaching, tailoring, and challenging customer perspectives to unlock new opportunities.

- Network & Territory Expertise : Deep relationships within the territory, including decision makers and influencers who can be leveraged to accelerate business.

title: Senior Legal Counsel Carbon Markets
description:
About Carbonfuture 

Carbonfuture provides the trust infrastructure that helps organizations meet their net-zero commitments and gets climate action financed at scale. Our digital infrastructure makes carbon removal credits traceable, enforceable, and trustworthy, so suppliers, buyers, and financial institutions can transact with confidence.

Today, we are the global market leader by facilitated carbon removal sales volume, working with some of the most ambitious companies in the market, including Microsoft, Swiss Re, and SAP. We are backed by SIX, operator of the Swiss and Spanish stock exchanges, as a strategic investor and partner, and operate from our headquarters in Freiburg, Germany (Carbonfuture GmbH), where contracts are governed under German law. We also have subsidiaries in Switzerland and the US.

Your Role 

Our goal is to turn carbon credits into a new financial asset class and provide the settlement infrastructure. This requires governance frameworks for our digital infrastructure, standardised contracts for an evolving asset class and enforceable rules that financial institutions, regulators and customers can rely on, and Carbonfuture is writing many of them. The liability and risk landscape is largely unmapped: this is genuinely novel work where the legal groundwork you establish will set standards in an emerging industry. 

Our contracting parties span between project developers who are removing CO2 out of the atmosphere with frontier technologies as well as the biggest corporates worldwide (including SAP, Microsoft, Swiss Re) purchasing carbon credits from us. 

We're looking for a Senior Legal Counsel to lead that work. You'll own our contracts from first draft to signature, act as our legal lead in fundraising, and shape the legal and governance framework behind our instruments. You'll have the opportunity to publish, represent Carbonfuture in trade associations, and help define standards for the asset class. 

This is a senior, hands-on role with real ownership. You'll report to our COO, lead our in-house legal function including a part-time legal counsel, and own the legal budget. 

Key Responsibilities 

Contracts & Negotiation 

- Own the full contract lifecycle, from drafting and negotiation to signing, across customer, supplier, offtake and vendor agreements 

- Negotiate key deals together with leadership, bringing in external counsel where it adds value 

- Help build the standardised contract structure that replaces today's bespoke bilateral terms between suppliers and buyers and makes the markets scaleable 

Carbon Credits as a new Financial Asset Class 

- Drive the legal workstream to establish carbon credits as an institutional asset class, from governance framework to documentation 

- Advise on capital markets and regulatory questions as we work with institutional market participants, banks and supervisory authorities 

- Represent Carbonfuture in selected associations and help shape market standards through them 

Fundraising & Corporate 

- Act as our internal legal lead in fundraising rounds and own the signing and closing process 

- Manage shareholder matters and corporate governance 

- Select, brief and steer external law firms 

Compliance & Legal Operations 

- Oversee internal compliance across data protection, employment law and corporate governance 

- Own the legal budget, internal and external 

- Lead and develop a part-time legal counsel 

- Build templates, processes and playbooks so the wider team can handle routine legal questions independently 

What We're Looking For 

Experience: 

- 8+ years of legal experience, in-house, at a law firm, or ideally both 

- Deep expertise in German contract and commercial law, with hands-on experience in B2B transactions and negotiation 

- Deep expertise in German corporate law (Gesellschaftsrecht), knowledge of capital markets law (Kapitalmarktrecht) is considered a plus 

- Hands-on experience with financing rounds, M&A or comparable transactions, including signing and closing 

- Experience with European financial regulators such as BaFin, the ECB or FINMA is a strong advantage 

- A background in financial market infrastructure, banking, commodities or carbon markets is a plus; capital markets lawyers curious about climate are very welcome to apply 

Skills : 

- Fluent German and English, written and spoken, at a level that lets you negotiate and draft in both 

- You turn complex legal questions into clear options for the board, investors and colleagues who aren't lawyers 

- Sound commercial judgement: you calibrate risk to what's at stake and know when good enough is good enough 

- Confident negotiator who builds trust with counterparties, shareholders and external counsel 

- Self-directed: you spot problems early and solve them without waiting to be asked 

What We Offer 

- The chance to shape the legal foundations of a new asset class at a company already leading its market 

- A rapidly growing international team with a shared mission to address climate change 

- Flexible working hours and location. 

- Competitive salary 

- 30 days paid leave + bank holidays 

- Sports and Health benefits 

- Purpose-driven, ambitious colleagues and a friendly, open and inclusive environment 

Carbonfuture is an international hybrid and remote office environment with team members located in the EU, US and Latin America. Our main offices are located in Freiburg, Berlin, Zurich and San Francisco. Candidates should be prepared to either work from home or in one of our hubs. This position requires the ability to work core hours Monday through Friday with availability for European time zone meetings and events. This position will require occasional early morning or evening work and some in-person attendance for all-staff or department-level events which will require overnight travel. 

Candidates from cultures and backgrounds underrepresented in VC-backed startups and the climate space are strongly encouraged to apply. A diverse and inclusive workplace where we learn from each other is an integral part of our culture. We actively welcome people of different backgrounds, experiences, abilities, and perspectives. We are an equal-opportunity employer.

title: Product Manager, AI Driver
description:
Before the detail, here's the challenge you'd help us solve.

We build the embodied intelligence that moves real vehicles safely, and the ecosystem a billion machines will run on in the future. Very few people in AI can say this. Every role here, whatever the team, plugs into that.

Here’s what this particular role covers.

🛠️ About our Product Team 

Our Product team works at the intersection of AI research, engineering and customer needs to shape the future of autonomous driving at Wayve. We define product direction, translate complex technical capabilities into clear roadmaps, and bring cross-functional teams together to turn research into products that deliver real-world impact.

Working closely with engineers, researchers, programme managers and automotive partners, we balance long-term ambition with practical delivery. We combine technical depth with product judgement, listen carefully to our customers and teams, and create alignment around what to build, why it matters and how we’ll measure success.

🧠 Your day-to-day 

- Lead a cross-functional team of engineers, researchers and PMs without formal authority. Give them clarity, remove blockers, and motivate them through hard, ambiguous problems.

- Engage deeply with technical detail across AI / ML, autonomy and embodied AI. Debate trade-offs credibly with senior researchers and engineers, and bring structured thinking to complex technical decisions.

- Communicate crisply across audiences, from deep technical reviews with engineers, to executive updates with leadership, to customer-facing conversations.

- Listen actively to engineers, partners and customers, and turn what you hear into better decisions and stronger team alignment.

🧩 What you’ll be working on: 

- Independently own a substantial work package end-to-end. Define the problem, set the strategy, sequence the work, and lead the team to ship outcomes that move the AI Driver product forward.

- Translate R&D progress and customer needs into a clear product roadmap, sequencing capabilities to maximise impact and de-risk delivery.

- Set, track and report on clear KPIs and milestones, and establish the operating rhythm the team needs to deliver.

🙌 You should apply if: 

- You’ve independently owned a substantial work package and led a cross-functional team to deliver it. You take responsibility for outcomes and proactively work through blockers.

- You bring strong technical depth, ideally in AI/ML, autonomy, robotics or another deep-tech domain, and can engage credibly with senior engineers and researchers.

- You’re a careful listener and clear communicator who can motivate and energise a team through ambiguity.

- You have a proven track record in product management, technical programme management or a similar role working on complex, cutting-edge technical products.

- You work autonomously, exercise sound judgement and are comfortable making decisions with imperfect information, then adapting as you learn.

🌱 Not ticking every box? That’s totally okay! If you’re passionate about autonomy and keen to learn, we encourage you to apply even if you don’t meet every requirement.

More about Wayve: 

🚀 Wayve is building the leading AI platform for autonomous driving. We are pioneering an end to end AI approach that enables vehicles to learn directly from real world experience, developing the ability to adapt, generalise and improve at scale. Instead of relying on hand coded rules or pre mapped environments, our AI Driver learns to drive by understanding the world around it. The result is technology that navigates complex urban environments with intelligence, precision and natural flow, unlocking meaningful advances in both safety and efficiency. We believe autonomy represents a once in a generation transformation in how people and goods move, comparable to the shift from horses to cars, and from human driven vehicles to intelligent machines.

Our ambition is to make autonomy universal. Wayve’s mapless and hardware agnostic AI platform integrates with global OEM partners, enabling continuous software evolution and unlocking advanced levels of automation from L2 plus through to L4 as our core AI model scales. In a race increasingly defined by intelligence and real world learning, Wayve is taking a distinct approach, building a generalisable driving intelligence that can power any vehicle, anywhere. By combining embodied AI with scalable deployment, we are creating technology that can be shaped to each OEM brand and driver experience, accelerating the transition to a safer, more intelligent future of mobility.

How we work 💻- Locations & Flexible Working: 

Our main hubs are in London, Sunnyvale, Yokohama, Herzliya, Vancouver and Leonberg. We operate a hybrid working model that combines in-person collaboration in our dedicated office spaces with focused time working remotely. This gives our teams the connection and energy of working together, alongside the flexibility to do their best work in a way that fits their lives.

🔍 The Interview Process: 

Our process is clear and respectful of your time:

- Initial call / recruiter screen (30 mins)

- Competency Interviews (Product Sense interview; 1 hour)

- Deep-dive technical interviews (Cross-functional, domain-specific interview, presentation; 2.5 hours total)

- Final interview : mission & values alignment (1 hour).

We’ll always explain the format and work around your availability.

What’s in it for you (Location dependant): 

💰 Salaries benchmarked against the market annually
📈 Meaningful equity, sharing in the ownership and long term success of Wayve
✈️ Relocation support and visa sponsorship where applicable
✅ Hybrid working, core hours and the chance to work hands on in vehicle workshops and labs
📚 Learning and development budgets with support for training, conferences and growth
🩺 Comprehensive benefits including health insurance, dental, enhanced maternity and paternity leave, retirement or pension where applicable, access to therapists, wellbeing partnerships, team socials and more

A quick, honest note before you apply.

Wayve is not a mature, fully-structured place with the playbook already written. Much of how we work is still being written, and if you join, you’ll help write it. That suits people who want real ownership more than people who need a settled structure from day one.

If that sounds like the kind of problem you want to spend your time on, we’d really like to hear from you.

At Wayve we're committed to creating a diverse, fair and respectful culture that is inclusive of everyone based on their unique skills and perspectives, and regardless of sex, race, religion or belief, ethnic or national origin, disability, age, citizenship, marital, domestic or civil partnership status, sexual orientation, gender identity, veteran status, pregnancy or related condition (including breastfeeding) or any other basis as protected by applicable law.

For more information visit Careers at Wayve. To learn more about what drives us, visit Values at Wayve 

DISCLAIMER: We will not ask about marriage or pregnancy, care responsibilities or disabilities in any of our job adverts or interviews. However, we do look to capture information about care responsibilities, and disabilities among other diversity information as part of an optional DEI Monitoring form to help us identify areas of improvement in our hiring process and ensure that the process is inclusive and non-discriminatory.

title: Business Development Representative (BDR)
description:
Accelerating embodied AGI. 

The next ten years of AI will not be won in software. They will be won in the physical world: in factories, hospitals, kitchens, fields, and homes. The companies that own that data will own the century.

MicroAGI is building it. We are a data research and deployment lab. Atlas captures the manual work inside Europe’s industrial champions, trains foundation models on it, and deploys the right robot onto the floor, with no teleoperation and no interruption to the line. Shift records how physical work actually happens and turns it into training-ready data.

We were founded by former Formula 1 engineers from Red Bull Racing and Mercedes, together with a researcher from the Alan Turing Institute. Our $55M seed round, the largest in German history, was led by Hummingbird with Northzone, LocalGlobe, Village Global, and redalpine. We are based in Munich, with our research centre in Zürich and teams in London, New York, and Istanbul. We are now building the engineering and research teams that will take Atlas into new industries.

This is not a typical BDR seat. It is the chance to build our enterprise go-to-market from zero. Enterprises want to deploy humanoids. Your job is to find them, reach them first, and bring them in. The market, the outreach, and the first conversation are yours to build.

What You Will Do

- Own outreach and first contact. Bring the enterprises that want to deploy humanoids to us.

- Generate and qualify leads across enterprise accounts.

- Own one or more markets end to end. Your territory, your pipeline, your number.

- Continuously improve how we reach enterprise companies. New channels, new angles, kill what does not work.

- Book qualified meetings and hand over the context to close.

Requirements

- A track record of excellence, wherever you earned it: a top-tier VC, a startup, or a company you built yourself.

- Willing to get your hands dirty. You build the lists, write the emails, and chase the follow-ups yourself.

- High agency: you don't wait to be told what to do.

- Fluent in two languages.

- Based in Munich, in the office.

Nice to Have

- A strong academic background. We care more about what you have done than where you studied.

Who Will Thrive at MicroAGI

Everyone we hire is assessed on the same four traits:

- Intensity: you work at a pace that matches the size of the opportunity, and you sustain it.

- Entrepreneurial: you start things nobody asked for, and you finish them.

- Raw IQ: you learn fast, reason from first principles, and get sharper when the problem changes.

This is for you if: 

- You would rather own a problem end to end than wait for a spec.

- You use AI every day, and you can tell a correct answer from a plausible one.

- You want to work in person, in the office, with people who are very good at what they do.

This is not for you if: 

- You are looking for a predictable 9-to-5.

- You would forward output you cannot explain.

- "That’s not my job" feels like a reasonable answer.

How We Hire

We read every application and reply within five working days.

- Talent Screen (30 min): a first conversation, both ways.

- Technical or Functional Interview (60 min): how you think when the problem changes.

- Your Work (60 min): bring something you are proud of and walk us through it.

- Leadership (30 min): a conversation with our CEO.

- Coworking Day (engineering and research roles): a day building with the team on a real problem.

Then a decision, usually within a few days.

Pay Transparency

Compensation includes base salary and equity. The salary range for this role is shown on this posting.

What We Offer

- Agency: real ownership from day one, and decisions that actually matter.

- Freedom: to choose how you solve the problem, without layers of approval.

- A seat on a rocketship: one of Europe’s fastest-growing deep-tech companies, at the earliest stage.

Equal Opportunity

MicroAGI welcomes applications from everyone. We assess candidates on their work and potential, regardless of ethnic origin, gender, religion or belief, disability, age, or sexual identity.
